why:
phase-482 W4 (2026-10-07): `rclcpp_lifecycle::LifecycleNode` IS an `rclcpp::Node`, so this is `rclcpp::Node::get_graph_event`, inherited, with `cpp:Node::get_graph_event`'s contract. The extractor records only the members a class declares, so this key correlates as upstream-only even though the name resolves.

Before phase-482 W4: hands out the `Event` the next call to `wait_for_graph_change` blocks on. rclcpp's graph `Event` is a `shared_ptr`-held mutex+flag that a background graph LISTENER THREAD sets and `wait_for_graph_change` blocks on. Three constraints each rule the shape out: no allocator for the shared object (`make_shared` -- the same reason pubsub declines every `make_shared` factory), no background transport thread to run the listener (RFC-0002 puts one executor on one RTOS task and `rmw_vtable.h` says in its own words that no graph slot may block on the wire), and no blocking wait outside the executor (RFC-0021: a blocking helper takes the executor, as `rclc_client_wait_for_service` does). Our shape for "the graph changed" is an EDGE: the `node_get_graph_guard_condition` slot, deliberately `set_wake_callback`-shaped rather than a waitable, carrying no payload because delivering WHAT changed means buffering it. That slot is NULL in every backend, so nothing fires today. What a user loses: no way to be told that a node or an endpoint appeared or went away -- only `rclc_client_wait_for_service` / `Client::service_is_ready` answers that, and only for one service at a time. (CORRECTED 2026-09-04, phase-417: this cited `server_available`, which in C++ is now only a `[[deprecated]]` forwarder -- phase-379 W6 decision 2 settled the name as `service_is_ready`. C still exports both, which is what `c:client_server_available` records.) NOTE this contradicts the node stage's `c:node_get_graph_guard_condition`, which declines on "nothing would ever trigger it here"; the slot exists precisely so a backend CAN trigger it.
